identity.name: Kingdom of Hán (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Kingdom of Hán under Xiang Yu

land.text: the restored Hán of Han Cheng, whom Xiang Yu confirmed as king in 206

predecessors.note: The han dossier (ea-01) records the 208 restoration ('Han Cheng, a descendant of the royal family of Hán, was enthroned as King of Hán') from the Zhang Liang page; the pages opened here start at 206 ('Han Cheng was appointed as the King of Han', Cheng, King of Han page). Cliopatria's Han row ends in 207 and this row begins in 206.

land.text: the Hán vassal kingdom at its last seat, Taiyuan Commandery with its capital at Jinyang, 201

successors.note: The Xin of Han page says Hán Xin 'defected to the Xiongnu' in 201 and does not say who took the land; the Han Empire (han-dynasty) is the researcher's reading. The page's infobox gives his reign as 205-196 BC with successor 'Unknown'.

capitals.name: Yangzhai (Yuzhou, Henan)
capitals.note: The Xin of Han page gives 'the capital at Yangzhai' for Hán Xin's kingdom around Yingchuan; no page opened names the capital of Han Cheng's or Zheng Chang's Hán (the Zhang Liang page is silent). Coordinates are for modern Yuzhou, which is not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Jinyang (Taiyuan, Shanxi)
capitals.note: 'he relocated the Hán vassal kingdom to Taiyuan Commandery with the capital at Jinyang'; Hán Xin then asked for Mayi (Shuozhou) and 'the emperor approved his request'. Coordinates are Taiyuan's.

rulers.name: Han Cheng
rulers.note: Page: 'Han Cheng (died 206 BC)'; killed by Xiang Yu 'months later' than his appointment (late 206 per the Xiang Yu page).

rulers.name: Hán Xin (Xin of Han)
rulers.note: Infobox 'King of Hán 205 BC - 196 BC'; the reign here stops at the 201 defection to the Xiongnu.

keyframe_review.note: 86,684 km2 for 206-204 over southwestern Henan (bbox 110.5-115.3 E, 32.6-35.5 N), matching the table's 'Hán ... Han Cheng ... southwestern Henan'. No page opened gives an area, so there is no infobox figure to compare. This is Han Cheng's Hán, not Liu Bang's Hàn (Cliopatria's 'Han' row, 455,000 km2 in Sichuan and Shaanxi for 206-204). The kingdom outlives the row: see the new keyframes for 203-201.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 204, but the Xin of Han page keeps the Hán kingdom, as Hán Xin's 'vassal kingdom' of the Han, until the relocation to Taiyuan in 201. The page names Yingchuan and Yangzhai, not a boundary, so the outline is the 206-204 shape (southwestern Henan) carried forward on the researcher's reading. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the correction used the plain name Hán, which the gazetteer resolves by slug 'han' to both Cliopatria features alive in 204 (Han Cheng's Hán, 416 cells, and Liu Bang's Hàn, 1,925 cells); it now keeps only the Hán feature (east of 110.4 E), 416 cells.

The radius is the researcher's stand-in for the commandery; the page dates the move to 201 ('In 201 BC, Liu Bang realised that the Hán vassal kingdom was in a strategic location') and puts the defection to the Xiongnu in the same year.

region.text: southwestern Henan, the Hán of Han Cheng (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Han Cheng King of Hán in the Eighteen Kingdoms. Table: 'Hán (韩) ... Han Cheng (Hán royalty); southwestern Henan'; kingdoms 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'. The Han Cheng page: 'Han Cheng was appointed as the King of Han'; the Xiang Yu page dates the division 'In the spring of 206 BC'. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the region now keeps only the Hán feature (416 cells, 110.5-115.3 E); the plain name Hán had resolved by slug 'han' to Liu Bang's Hàn of Sichuan and Shaanxi as well (2,341 cells in all), which put Bashu in this dossier and set it against kingdom-of-han. Eighteen Kingdoms table re-read 2026-11-01: 'Hán' Han Cheng, 'southwestern Henan'; 'Hàn' Liu Bang, 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi'.

Late 206: Xiang Yu kills Han Cheng and puts Zheng Chang on the throne of Hán. 'In late 206 BC, Xiang Yu executed Han Cheng, the King of Hán, and replaced him with Zheng Chang.' The Timeline page has both steps under 206 BC; Zheng Chang is not Hán royalty, so the ruling house changes while the kingdom continues.

205: Hán Xin, with Liu Bang's backing, replaces Zheng Chang and the kingdom passes to Liu Bang's side. 'He was made King of Hán (韓王) in 205 BC by Liu Bang'; the Zheng Chang page: 'Later that year, Hán Xin attacked the Hán kingdom with support from Liu Bang and defeated Zheng Chang', who 'surrendered' (infobox reign ends 205). The Timeline page puts the conquest under 206 BC, the Chu-Han Contention page under 205; 205 is used because two pages give it. The land does not change; the Han dossiers hold the vassal tint.

region.text: southwestern Henan, the Hán of Han Cheng (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 201: the Yingchuan lands are given up when the kingdom is relocated. Page silent on the handover: the Xin of Han page says only that Hán Xin 'relocated the Hán vassal kingdom to Taiyuan Commandery'; that the old lands went back to the Han is the researcher's inference. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): same Hán-only region as ledger 0 (416 cells); the plain name had also resolved to Liu Bang's Hàn.

201: the Hán kingdom is relocated to Taiyuan Commandery, capital Jinyang (Hán Xin later asks for Mayi, approved). The page dates the move: 'In 201 BC, Liu Bang realised that the Hán vassal kingdom was in a strategic location' and relocated it (reviewer, 2026-10-19: confidence raised from 2).
201: the court moves from Yangzhai to Jinyang. 'he relocated the Hán vassal kingdom to Taiyuan Commandery with the capital at Jinyang'.

region.text: the Hán kingdom at Taiyuan after Hán Xin's defection

ledger.note: 201: Hán Xin defects to the Xiongnu and the kingdom of Hán ends. 'In 201 BC, after he was suspected of conspiring with the Xiongnu against the Hàn Empire, he defected to the Xiongnu'; the Xiongnu 'attacked Mayi' shortly before. The infobox lists his reign as 205-196 BC (he was killed in 196), with successor 'Unknown'; the end of the kingdom in 201 is the researcher's reading of the defection.

wars.name: Chu-Han Contention
wars.outcome: Han victory (infobox '206-202 BCE'). Hán passed from Xiang Yu's nominee Zheng Chang to Liu Bang's ally Hán Xin without a change of outline.
wars.note: The Chu-Han Contention page has Hán 'refused to submit to Liu Bang, so Liu Bang sent' Han Xin in 205; no border moved, so no zone is listed.

certainty.note: The kingdoms were assigned by Xiang Yu from commanderies, with no survey or treaty lines; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation and the Taiyuan year is a radius.

notes:
Slug collision: this is 'Hán' (-206..-204), Han Cheng's kingdom in southwestern Henan; 'Han' (-404..-203) is the Warring States Han (slug han, ea-01) and its Cliopatria row also carries Liu Bang's Hàn of 206-203 (455,000 km2 in Sichuan and Shaanxi), which the group's kingdom-of-han dossier takes. Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve rows (dai, jibei, chang-shan, han-2, henan, jiaodong, jiujiang, liaodong, linjiang, sai, yin, yong): they are different kingdoms with different kings, not one state; each keeps its own dossier.
Dates: the Timeline page puts Hán Xin's conquest under 206, the Chu-Han Contention and Xin of Han pages under 205. The Xin of Han page makes the kingdom live to 201 (relocation to Taiyuan, defection), which Cliopatria (ends 204) does not show; the extension rests on that one page. The vassal tint for 205-201 belongs to the Han dossiers (kingdom-of-han has no vassal_start for han-2).
Gazetteer: Yangzhai (Yuzhou, Henan) is not in places.jsonl; Jinyang resolves through Taiyuan. Capital of Han Cheng's reign is not stated on any page opened. fx-25 (2026-11-01): the ledger found and loss regions and the 203 keyframe use cliopatria 'Hán', which the gazetteer slugifies to 'han' and resolves to every Cliopatria feature of that slug alive in the year, Liu Bang's Hàn included; they now intersect with a polygon east of 110.4 E that keeps only Han Cheng's Hán (416 cells).
